JNJ.rationale: JNJ is a structurally sound healthcare franchise with strong pipeline execution (TALVEY Phase 3, IMAAVY Phase 2/3, Firefly Bio acquisition) and stable ~$24B quarterly revenue. However, the quantitative picture is decisively negative across all three pillars. Pillar 1 (fundamentals): margins are deteriorating sharply — operating margin compressed from 31.2% to 24.9% QoQ, gross margin fell 330bps, and operating cash flow collapsed 72.6% from $9.17B to $2.51B. TTM earnings are contaminated by a one-time Q1 gain (62.3% operating margin on $21.89B revenue), and normalized annualized net income is ~$21B vs the TTM headline of $26.9B. Pillar 2 (valuation): PE has expanded 58% from 16.8x to 26.5x over 12 months while net margin declined from 24.4% to 21.8% and ROE from 27.9% to 25.9%. The 3.8% earnings yield sits 66bps below the 10-year Treasury at 4.46%, offering negative equity risk premium. The market is paying peak multiples for declining profitability. Pillar 3 (near-term catalyst): the Q1 one-time gain will roll off TTM in coming quarters, mechanically depressing reported earnings and likely triggering multiple compression. Patent cliffs (STELARA erosion accelerating, Simponi/Opsumit LOEs imminent) and unresolved talc litigation (75,000+ lawsuits, fresh $10.2M verdict) add downside risk. The franchise quality is real but the price has overshot the fundamental trajectory — this is a quality business at an unattractive price with a clear de-rating catalyst ahead.
